summary: Ran the one-off configs/accounts.yml -> DB migration for real (previously blocked on a password for the new User row). Created 1 User, 2 Strategy rows (S007/CTRADER, S009/BYBIT), 2 Account rows (CTRADER demo, BYBIT mainnet), and 2 AccountStrategy links with initial_balance seeded from accounts.yml. APP_SECRET_KEY must be exported from .env manually before running this script -- it does not load .env itself, same as the rest of webapp/.

Installed and loaded the S009 launchd scheduler (com.algo.s009-paper), which had never actually been running: no plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents, no launchd job, no cron entry -- since the last manual run on 2026-08-06 the paper ledger/state had gone stale (last_day stuck at 2026-08-05) while 4 real positions sat open on the dedicated Bybit-algo009 mainnet account with nothing auto-rebalancing them. Fixed a real bug this exposed in scripts/s009_tick.py: tick() defaulted its now parameter to timezone-aware UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)), but utils/trade_logger.py writes event timestamp fields as naive local time, so _has_event_today's since-cutoff comparison raised "can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes" on every idle tick once a heartbeat had already been logged for the day -- same failure signature as the two "S009 cycle subprocess exited non-zero" entries already in S009.log from 2026-08-03. Changed the default to naive local time (matching the logger and scripts/s007_tick.py's own default); this now parameter only affects heartbeat dedup/log-file day-naming, not the actual UTC trading-day boundary (_expected_last_closed_day() is independent of it). Added tests/scripts/test_s009_tick.py (regression test replays the exact two-consecutive-idle-ticks crash, plus branch coverage for the needs-cycle/timeout/nonzero-exit/state-did-not-advance paths, mirroring tests/scripts/test_s007_tick.py's structure). Per explicit user confirmation, also switched deployment/com.algo.s009-paper.plist from --broker off (shadow-only) to --broker execute --allow-mainnet, so the scheduler now auto-rebalances the real mainnet book daily; verified via BybitExec.positions()/wallet_equity() (read-only) that the reload itself placed no orders.

Replaced the S007-specific Ofelia job-run label with one generic, permanent dispatcher job (docker-compose.yml's 'dispatch' job runs scripts/scheduler_tick.py every minute). The dispatcher reads deployment/schedule.yml (strategies[].schedule / tasks[].command+schedule, 5-field cron matched via croniter) and subprocess-invokes `webapp.runner --strategy <name>` or a task's command when due -- adding a strategy's cadence or a background job is now a schedule.yml edit + code review, never a docker-compose.yml change. Deliberately config-file-based, not a DB table: a task always references a script that has to be written anyway, so a DB row would not actually enable 'add without redeploy'. Verified end-to-end on Podman: image rebuilds with croniter, a simulated in-window Monday timestamp correctly triggered a real S007 cycle through the container (log + account_strategies.last_cycle_at both updated), and Ofelia registers/fires the new job. Found and fixed a real doc/image mismatch along the way: the actual pulled mcuadros/ofelia:latest fires a 5-field '* * * * *' schedule EVERY SECOND, not every minute, contradicting its own README's 'seconds optional in 0.4.x+' claim -- Ofelia's own outer schedule needed the 6-field seconds-first form ('0 * * * * *'); this is separate from and does not affect schedule.yml's 5-field croniter strings, which are a different parser entirely.

Found and fixed a serious live incident: the Podman machine VM (hosting the Ofelia scheduler container since yesterday's S007 cutover) does not reliably resume its internal clock after the host Mac wakes from sleep. Its clock froze at 2026-08-09 14:07 (last real firing) and stayed 18+ hours behind while `podman ps`/`podman machine inspect` both kept reporting it healthy/running -- Ofelia's cron scheduler silently stopped firing S007/S009 dispatch with zero errors anywhere. This meant S007 had NO live coverage at all overnight (legacy launchd unloaded yesterday, new Docker path silently dead) until caught this morning before the 10:00 Kyiv session. `chronyc makestep` / restarting chronyd inside the VM did not fix it -- only a full `podman machine stop` + `start` resynced the clock. Fix: scripts/podman_healthcheck.py, installed as a launchd job (deployment/com.algo.podman-healthcheck.plist, every 5 min via StartCalendarInterval) -- launchd supervises the Docker/Podman layer from OUTSIDE it, since launchd is the one layer already proven immune to this Mac's sleep/wake cycles. Compares host vs VM epoch; beyond a 120s threshold, restarts the machine + `docker compose up -d ofelia` and verifies the fix took. Caught and fixed a real bug in the fix itself before trusting it: subprocess.run(['podman', ...]) failed silently under launchd's minimal PATH (no /opt/podman/bin), misreported as 'machine unreachable' -- switched to the absolute binary path. Verified live: detected a real 207s drift immediately after the manual machine restart and self-healed correctly; a second run confirmed the fixed PATH issue with a clean, quiet (healthy) exit. 6 new tests, full suite (78) green. Per user decision: S009's DB-driven path stays broker='off' (deferred) until this reliability gap was closed -- this incident is exactly why that caution was right.

Fixed two real bugs found live during S007 first trading day on the new Docker/Ofelia path: (1) dispatch job-run container ran in UTC instead of Europe/Kyiv (missing TZ env on the label), causing S007 to silently skip its 10:00-13:00 Kyiv session window; (2) scheduler_tick had no overlap guard, so a slow cycle (55-118s, observed live) let two dispatch ticks run the same strategy concurrently -- added a per-(kind,name) file lock under data/.scheduler_locks with stale-lock self-healing. Also fixed podman_healthcheck.py: the watchdog previously treated a fully-unreachable (stopped) machine as non-healable and did nothing, leaving zero dispatch coverage for 25+ minutes live during an open real position; now both drift and unreachable trigger the same heal path, and each heal step is wrapped so a failing subprocess call cannot crash the healthcheck itself. Root cause of the recurring Podman-machine instability (3 outages in ~2.5h today) remains unexplained -- watchdog now reacts correctly to all observed failure modes but does not fix why the VM keeps dying.

Fully deactivated the legacy launchd path for S007 (Trello: "Развести Ofelia и launchd-агент com.anton.algo.s007bot", Tier-1). Removed the installed plist from ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ (was already unloaded since the 2026-08-09 Docker cutover, but still one launchctl load away from an accident -- both paths independently manage the same demo account ctrader-47939312). Added explicit DEPRECATED headers to scripts/s007_tick.py and the tracked scripts/com.anton.algo.s007bot.plist explaining the manual break-glass recovery procedure (docker compose down ofelia FIRST, then reinstall+load), and updated docker-compose.yml comment accordingly. No code logic changed, only docs/comments + removing the installed artifact; 51 tests still pass.

Added the Deribit BTC+ETH option-board daily snapshot collector (ALGODEV-9), implemented against claude/infra-scheduled-jobs-spec.md rev.2 SS3: scripts/fetch_deribit_snapshot.py joins public/get_book_summary_by_currency + public/get_instruments per currency, writes data/raw/deribit_options/date=YYYY-MM-DD/{BTC,ETH}.parquet atomically (temp file + os.replace), and is watermark-driven via utils/strategy_state.py::FileStateStore (data/state/deribit_snapshot.json, separate last_attempt_ts/last_snapshot_date) since a missed day cannot be backfilled -- no --since/--until on purpose. Exit codes 0/1/2 (ok-or-noop/transient/fatal-contract); --dry-run/--force/--with-greeks flags. Deliberately does not store delta/bid_iv/ask_iv/moneyness/time-to-expiry by default (recomputable from raw fields; --with-greeks is the opt-in escape hatch). Code and 12 tests were written in a sandbox without access to the real .venv; re-ran both pytest and ruff here for real (12 passed, lint clean) before trusting them. Added pyarrow==24.0.0 to requirements-docker.txt (needed inside the algo-worker image once this task is scheduled), wrote docs/DERIBIT_OPTIONS_SNAPSHOT.md (parquet schema v1), and added the deployment/schedule.yml tasks: entry (name: deribit_snapshot, schedule '0 19 * * *' = 16:00 UTC at the current EEST/UTC+3 offset; documented in-file that this drifts to 17:00 UTC once Kyiv falls back to EET/UTC+2, a manual twice-a-year adjustment). Deliberately did NOT touch docker-compose.yml (task scope excludes it) and held off on git-committing pending Anton's explicit confirmation that the Ofelia-vs-launchd(com.anton.algo.s007bot) scheduler conflict is resolved before treating this as ready for real deploy.

Migrated S009's real-money execution off its legacy launchd path onto the DB-driven Docker/Ofelia path, per Anton's explicit decision (previously webapp/runner.py::_worker_s009 hardcoded broker='off' unconditionally, per the 2026-08-10 note that enabling real orders there was 'a separate, explicit decision to make later'). Added AccountStrategy.broker_mode ('off'/'dry'/'execute', default 'off', migration 004) so real-order gating is per (account,strategy) link, not a single global switch -- flipping Bybit-algo009's S009 link to 'execute' cannot silently promote the second registered S009 account (Bybit-tradebot1, left 'off'). _worker_s009 now also requires Account.env=='mainnet' before allow_mainnet=True, mirroring bot/bybit_exec.py::BybitExec's own guard. Verified end-to-end against the live account before cutover: ran the real worker with broker_mode='dry' (real credentials, real Bybit mainnet equity fetch, no orders placed) and confirmed the computed rebalance plan (close stale ATOM position, open TRX/INJ/DOGE/NEAR) matched what the legacy launchd path had already computed today, then flipped to 'execute'. Decommissioned the legacy path: unloaded launchd job com.algo.s009-paper (via scripts/s009_tick_install.sh uninstall) after confirming today's real rebalance had already settled through it (loop_settled today=2026-08-13, so no coverage gap before the DB path's next scheduled run), and added DEPRECATED headers to scripts/s009_tick.py + deployment/com.algo.s009-paper.plist mirroring S007's 2026-08-10 deprecation pattern exactly (break-glass fallback only, explicit warning not to run both paths against the same account at once). Rebuilt algo-worker:latest (picking up this change plus ALGODEV-9's Deribit snapshot collector and other already-tree-resident work, per Anton's explicit choice to rebuild with all uncommitted WIP as-is) and smoke-tested the new image directly (pyarrow import, scripts.fetch_deribit_snapshot import, schedule.yml task/strategy parsing, webapp.runner + BrokerMode import) plus confirmed a live Ofelia dispatch tick against it succeeds. 27 webapp tests pass (24 pre-existing + 3 new broker_mode-gating cases); ruff clean on all touched files.

Fixed ALGODEV-9 Deribit snapshot job: fetch_instruments passed expired=False (Python bool) to requests, which serializes it as the query string "False" (capital F) -- Deribit public/get_instruments rejects anything but lowercase "true"/"false" and returned HTTP 400 on every real invocation, even though the fully-mocked test suite passed. Found by actually running the job end-to-end in the algo-worker Podman image (checking whether the deployment/schedule.yml-wired job works per Jira ALGODEV-9), not by the unit tests. Changed the param to the literal string "false"; rebuilt the image and re-ran live against the real Deribit API -- now writes BTC.parquet (794 rows) and ETH.parquet (670 rows) under data/raw/deribit_options/date=2026-08-13/, and a second run correctly no-ops via the watermark (skip_already_captured).

Hardened the Podman-machine watchdogs heal routine after repeated live instability today (host swap at ~94%, machine flapping unreachable every few minutes for hours). Found two real gaps: (1) machine start sometimes falls back to a per-start temp Docker-API-forwarding socket instead of /var/run/docker.sock (podman logs Another process was listening...) -- podman compose up -d ofelia then fails outright with no DOCKER_HOST pointed at that path, so a heal could clock-sync successfully while ofelia stayed down the whole time; (2) the old healed verdict only checked VM clock drift, never whether ofelia itself was actually running, so this exact silent-partial-heal was possible and had already happened at least once live. Added _compose_env() (reads the ACTUAL bound socket path via machine inspect, sets DOCKER_HOST accordingly) and _ofelia_running() (a real podman ps check), used both for the main compose call and a one-shot retry if ofelia still is not up afterward; healed now requires clock_ok AND ofelia_ok. Rewrote tests/scripts/test_podman_healthcheck.py to dispatch fake subprocess responses by command instead of a fragile positional sequence (the old shape could not represent the new inspect/ps calls), added 2 new tests for both gaps; verified both fail against the pre-fix code and pass after. Verified live: manual machine stop/start + podman compose up -d ofelia, confirmed DOCKER_HOST resolution against the real machine inspect output, S007 dispatch resumed.
